locator: I q.3 a.4 co., second proof: esse est actualitas omnis formae vel naturae: non enim bonitas vel humanitas significatur in actu, nisi prout significamus eam esse
interpretation: Being is the actuality of every form or nature: goodness or humanity is not signified as in act except insofar as we signify it to be. Read as the consequence formalized by STMT-ACTUALITY-ONLY-INSOFAR-AS-BEING: whatever is in act in some respect has being. The sentence is put in terms of signification ('significatur', 'significamus'); the reading takes it, as the proof's next step does ('oportet igitur quod ipsum esse comparetur ad essentiam ... sicut actus ad potentiam'), as a claim about things, not only about speech. The proof's use of it, that in God essence is esse, is not part of this statement. A further witness beside q.4 a.1 ad 3 (AQUINAS-ST-I-Q4-A1-AD3-ACTUALITY-AS-BEING-A); it is not a more basic premise.
